$schema_purpose: Deterministic, hard-constraint output format for the confirmed Table Definitions Word document produced by rdlc-coach-semantic-model. Every value here is a strict compliance requirement, not a stylistic suggestion. Pair with references/gold-example/ for a visual reference.

small_text_variant.purpose: Use a reduced table_text_size (see typography.column_table_text_size_half_points) specifically for 5-column technical/business column tables, since standard body table size does not comfortably fit 5 columns on a US Letter page.

column_table_schema.purpose: The required column structure for every table/column listing in Sections 4 (Dimensional Model Definitions) and 5 (Fact Table Definition). Introduced in v1.2 to separate the Fabric-physical name from the Power BI-facing name, per Microsoft skills-for-fabric naming-conventions.md.

column_definitions.Technical Name (Fabric): The physical column name as it exists in the Fabric Lakehouse/Warehouse and as ETL builds it. Retains existing data-engineering convention (e.g., no-space casing). Used as the TMDL sourceColumn mapping for Step 13.
column_definitions.Business Name (Power BI): The display name exposed in the built Power BI semantic model. Must follow naming-conventions.md: readable casing with spaces, no CamelCase/snake_case/UPPER_CASE, no technical prefixes (Fact_, Dim_, DIM_, FACT_, STG_).
column_definitions.Type: Data type using Fabric/DAX-aware terminology (e.g., Int64, Decimal, String, DateTime) — not generic terms like 'Integer' or 'Text'. Never use Double; use Decimal or Int64 instead.
column_definitions.Description: Business-language description of what the column represents. Defines any acronyms used in the name.
column_definitions.Build Notes: Optional. Populate only when relevant: 'Hidden — key column', 'Hidden — FK column', 'Hidden — base column for explicit measure', 'Hidden — backend/QA only', 'SummarizeBy: None', 'dataCategory: "..."', 'sortByColumn: ...'. Leave blank rather than writing 'N/A' when no build note applies.

table_naming_requirements.purpose: Applies to every table introduced in Sections 4 and 5. Table-level heading format: '<Business Name>  (technical: <Technical Name>)'.
business_name_rules: No technical prefixes: Fact_, Dim_, FACT_, DIM_, STG_ are forbidden in the Business Name.
Fact tables: plural business name (e.g., 'Animal Intakes', 'Sales', 'Orders').
The primary descriptive column of a dimension should prefer a Business Name matching the table's own name (e.g., 'Centre' inside the Centre table) rather than repeating '<Table> Name'.
technical_name_rules: Retains whatever data-engineering/Fabric convention is already established for the project (e.g., existing Fact_/Dim_ prefixes are acceptable here, since this name never appears in the Power BI Fields pane).

hidden_and_build_property_requirements.purpose: These are Fabric/TOM-level build properties, not structural design decisions. They are recorded in the Build Notes column (per-row) and, where they apply model-wide, summarized in the required 'Fabric / Power BI Build Notes Summary' section.
must_flag_hidden: Every primary key column on every dimension table
Every foreign key column on the fact table
Every fact-table base column that has a corresponding explicit DAX measure (the measure is the user-facing interface, not the raw column)
Any natural/reconciliation-only key retained purely for backend QA (e.g., a source system transaction ID)
hidden_and_build_property_requirements.must_flag_summarize_by_none: Any numeric column not meant to be aggregated by a report author by default — date keys, calendar year/month numbers, postal codes, and similar identifier-like numerics.
hidden_and_build_property_requirements.fact_table_surrogate_key_rule: Do not include a surrogate primary key column on a fact table. A natural/source system key is sufficient to guarantee grain uniqueness; a fact-level surrogate key is memory overhead with no join benefit in a columnstore (VertiPaq) engine. If a draft table definition includes one, flag it for removal during review rather than carrying it into the confirmed document.

note_box_convention.purpose: Used to flag material changes from a prior document version, accepted risks, deferred scope items, or explicitly assumed/unconfirmed decisions.
required_prefix_patterns: Assumed — user deferred to reviewer recommendation, pending validation:

required_section_order: 2. Naming Convention — Technical vs. Business Names
7. Fabric / Power BI Build Notes Summary

must_state: Definition of Technical Name (Fabric) vs. Business Name (Power BI)
That DAX formulas and relationship descriptions elsewhere in the document reference Business Names, since that is what is queryable in the built model
That Technical Names exist to let Step 13 (Implementation Agent) correctly map sourceColumn during build

per_table_required_elements: Table heading in format: '<Business Name>  (technical: <Technical Name>)' — see table_naming_requirements
Grain statement (dimensions state grain when not one-row-per-natural-entity)
Build/source location statement (e.g., 'built upstream in Fabric')
Driver Coverage statement (which named BRD/Discovery driver this table supports)
Column table following column_table_schema (5 columns: Technical Name | Business Name | Type | Description | Build Notes)
Note box for any change from a prior version, if applicable

required_elements: Table heading in format: '<Business Name>  (technical: <Technical Name>)'
Grain statement as an explicit business-event sentence (never a key list)
Foreign Keys list using Business Names (e.g., 'Date Key → Date')
Explicit statement of which measures are additive and their aggregation function
No fact-table surrogate primary key — see hidden_and_build_property_requirements.fact_table_surrogate_key_rule
Note box explaining any measure type correction (e.g., Boolean to Integer) if applicable

kpi_section_requirements.formula_naming: KPI formulas must reference Business Names in DAX syntax as they will appear in the built model (e.g., SUM('Animal Intakes'[Foster Flag])), not Technical Names.
kpi_section_requirements.ratio_kpis_must_state: Implemented as a DAX measure, not stored/pre-calculated
kpi_section_requirements.measure_naming_convention: Follow naming-conventions.md: '#' prefix for count measures is optional but consistent; percentage/rate measures use a '(%)' suffix; format string must be specified (e.g., "0.00%").

fabric_build_notes_summary_section_requi.purpose: A single consolidated section (Section 7) listing all Fabric/TOM build properties mentioned across the document's column tables, so Step 13 has one place to read build-readiness guidance rather than needing to scan every table.
must_include: Statement that key/FK columns are hidden across all tables
Statement that fact measure base columns are hidden in favor of explicit DAX measures
List of columns with SummarizeBy: None
Statement confirming no fact-table surrogate key
Recommendation on discourageImplicitMeasures model property, if explicit-measures-only design is confirmed

must_list: Any upstream document (BRD/Discovery Framework) corrections still needed
Any deferred/parked scope items with reasoning
Any 'Assumed — pending validation' items carried from the grilling session
Any unconfirmed cross-phase assumptions flagged during review

verification_step.instruction: After generating the .docx, render it to PDF and rasterize pages to visually verify table formatting, color application, and section order before presenting it as final output.
